newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas continues climb on SW heat, outage.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas continues climb on SW heat, outage.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were mostly stronger Wednesday, boosted by an outage in New Mexico and continuing heat in the Southwest, industry sources said.
Swing prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes gained about three cents to the high-$1.70s to mid-$1.80s per million British thermal units, indicating an increase of about 15 cents from last Wednesday.
In south Texas, prices were also firm in the mid-to-high $1.70s as a strong air-conditioning demand spurred more incremental buying.

El Paso Natural Gas reported earlier today that it experienced a pipeline failure late Tuesday about 30 miles north of Roswell, N.M., affecting about 550 million cubic feet per day. The company could not yet comment on when repairs would be complete.

As a result of the outage and warm Southwest temperatures, Permian basin prices edged up at least five cents to the mid-to-high $1.60s. The differential to Waha was constant as gas sold in the $1.70s.
The Midcontinent market was also feeling the brunt of the El Paso outage as traders reported closing deals in the high-$1.60s to mid-$1.70s, up a couple of cents from Tuesday.
Prices at the Detroit city-gate were talked in the low-$2 area, while Chicago city-gate gas was selling in the mid-to-high $1.80s.
